faq.title: Questions about dummy flight tickets
faq.lead: Short, honest answers before you order.

what.q: What is a dummy flight ticket?
what.a: A dummy flight ticket is a flight reservation with a booking reference (PNR) that shows your planned route and dates. It is not a paid airline ticket, so you do not buy a seat. Visa applicants use it as proof of onward or return travel.

legal.q: Is a dummy flight ticket legal?
legal.a: Using a flight reservation as a travel itinerary is common in visa applications. You must never present it as a purchased ticket or misstate your plans, and you should always follow what your embassy or consulate asks for. The decision on your visa is always theirs.

verify.a: Each itinerary carries a booking reference (PNR) and the flight details in a standard layout. How an individual airline or office checks a booking can differ, so we cannot promise how a specific officer will verify it.

accepted.a: Many applicants use flight reservations, but every embassy sets its own rules and we cannot guarantee acceptance or a visa. Read the checklist for your visa category before you order.

time.q: How fast do I receive it?
time.a: After your order is confirmed, your itinerary is sent to your email as a PDF. The delivery time for your plan is shown at checkout.

refund.a: Refund terms are shown at checkout before you pay, so you can read them first.

change.q: Can I change names or dates?
change.a: If something is wrong or your plans change, contact support with your order reference and we will tell you what can be updated for your plan.

pay.a: Payment options are shown at checkout. You pay for the reservation document only, never for the airline ticket itself.
